subject.title: [Bug]: Clarify Telegram channel_post auth when groups[chatId].allowFrom is configured

question: For Telegram channel_post native commands, should a configured groups[chatId].allowFrom sender allowlist be ignored in favor of explicit chat allow, or should channel_post fail closed as unsupported when sender-scoped auth is configured?
rationale: Telegram channel_post can lack a normal human sender, and current OpenClaw docs/code model groups[chatId].allowFrom as sender-scoped authorization, so automation cannot safely choose the security semantics.

options.title: Fail closed on sender-scoped allowFrom
options.body: Treat channel_post commands as unsupported when per-chat sender allowFrom is configured, return a clear denial or diagnostic, and document that a human sender is unavailable on this surface.

options.title: Use explicit chat allow only
options.body: Permit channel_post native commands from explicitly allowed channel chats and document that sender-scoped allowFrom is intentionally ignored for channel posts.

options.title: Defer to broader bot-to-bot policy
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader Telegram bot-to-bot policy work settles channel identity, peer-bot, and loop-control semantics together.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on sender-scoped allowFrom
recommendation.body: Treat channel_post commands as unsupported when per-chat sender allowFrom is configured, return a clear denial or diagnostic, and document that a human sender is unavailable on this surface.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest inspected history on Telegram sender-id auth and the docs where the final security policy should be encoded.
